title: Procedural texturing layer — panel seams + body decals + stripe/spot patterns (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-21-004)
intent: S102 deferred procedural texturing with the rationale 'no immediate consumer until gameplay shells demand visual variety beyond palette + shape'. That consumer now exists: GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration) put procbomber bombers into Kaboom Crew gameplay, and GDP-2026-05-22-003 added accessories. After playtesting the migrated game, the bombers read as 'a flat-coloured robot' rather than as the industrial-diorama identity the visual-style.md aims at. Adding panel seams + decals + procedural patterns is the highest-value visual upgrade we can ship without an artist. Pure additive layer on top of the existing 8-channel palette + 10-mesh tree.
rationale: Source: deferred proposal GDP-2026-05-21-004 (S102 notes: 'deferred — no immediate consumer'). Conditions for un-defer met: migration shipped (S104), accessories shipped (S106), recipe is formalised (S104), bombers are in production gameplay. Visual-style.md §3 declared 9 shader profiles including these layers; this story implements three of them on the character mesh path. Re-promote with acceptance hints rewritten under the post-S106 reality: paint paths now operate on the per-part mesh builders from S102 PROCBOMBER-PART-BUILDERS, not on the merged v0 generator.
acceptanceHints: Layer 1 — Panel seams (default-on, cheap):
Per-mesh, the 8 corner vertices of each BoxGeometry get the channel colour × 0.85 instead of the full channel; result is a soft 'panel edge' read on every face.

Implementation: extend examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/bomber-parts.ts paintVertexColors() to support a per-vertex Y-position test for the bottom-shadow trick (already there from S102 8-channel palette) PLUS a per-vertex corner test for seams.
Recipe toggle: `recipe.texturing.panelSeams: boolean` (default true). Schema entry added to CharacterRecipe.
Affects ALL part shapes (box / cylinder / capsule) — cylinder + capsule corners are interpreted as 'extreme vertices' (top + bottom edges) and get the same × 0.85 treatment.
Layer 2 — Body decals (opt-in, drives identity):
Three starter decals, each implemented as an emissive vertex-colour mask at a fixed anchor on a specific part-mesh:
chestEmblem  — 0.15-wide square centred on the FRONT face of the torso. Emissive = palette.accent.
helmetStripe — horizontal band across the top half of the head's vertical extent. Emissive = palette.accent.
kneePad      — small square on the FRONT face of each lowerLeg's upper third. Emissive = palette.handFoot (non-emissive, just a colour shift).
Each decal adds ONE Float32Array attribute per affected mesh (`decalEmissive`, 1 float per vertex, 0..1).
Shader extension: examples/kaboom-crew/src/shaders/ (or wherever the bomber material lives) gains a `uDecalEmissiveStrength` uniform + the per-vertex attribute sampling. ~30 LOC of GLSL.
Recipe field: `recipe.texturing.decals: ('chestEmblem'|'helmetStripe'|'kneePad')[]` — 0..3 picked deterministically from seed when unspecified.
Layer 3 — Stripe / spot patterns (opt-in, family flavour):
Shader-side procedural pattern: a second colour from palette.torsoAccent mixed in at a worley-dot or axial-stripe noise pattern driven by mesh local coordinates.
Stripe = sin(localY * scale) > 0.5 → blend torsoAccent in; otherwise base colour.
Spot = hash(floor(localXZ * scale)) % 4 == 0 → blend torsoAccent.
Solid = no blend (current behaviour).
Recipe field: `recipe.texturing.pattern: { style: 'solid' | 'stripes' | 'spots', scale: 0.5..3.0 } | undefined` (default undefined = solid).
Each palette family in bomber-palette.ts gains a default pattern bias (e.g. `ember` defaults to stripes, `mint` defaults to spots, `slate` stays solid). Recipe can override.
Family-default decal selection: each palette family also gains a default decal-pick rule — e.g. `ember` families lean toward `chestEmblem`, `mint` toward `helmetStripe`. Recipe overrides.
VALIDATION: recipe.texturing block is fully optional. Within texturing, decals enum strict; pattern.style enum strict; pattern.scale clamped to range. panelSeams is plain boolean.
BENCH UI: add three sections to the grouped panel from S103:
'Texturing → Panel seams' (toggle)
'Texturing → Decals' (3 checkboxes)
'Texturing → Pattern' (dropdown solid|stripes|spots + scale slider)
Each control writes to the recipe; rebuild fires the geometry-paint pass.

ACCESSORIES INTERACTION: accessories from S106 keep painting from their existing palette channels. The procedural-pattern shader does NOT extend to accessories — accessory meshes stay solid-coloured. Rationale: silhouette readability — decals + patterns on the body itself, accent dots on accessories, the eye doesn't get overloaded.
PERFORMANCE:
Vertex attribute additions: one extra Float32Array (`decalEmissive`) per affected mesh. ~24 floats × 6 affected meshes × 4 bombers = 576 extra floats total per arena. Negligible.

Shader uniform additions: 4 new uniforms (uPanelSeamStrength, uDecalEmissive, uPatternStyle, uPatternScale, uPatternColor). All within MeshStandardMaterial onBeforeCompile injection, no new material instance per bomber.
Steady-state per-frame cost is zero — attributes don't re-upload unless the recipe changes.
DETERMINISM: same seed + same texturing block → bit-identical vertex-colour + vertex-mask buffers. Test 50 seeds with random texturing combinations.

ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST: load two browser tabs with `?recipe=<base64-with-chestEmblem-stripes>` vs `?recipe=<base64-with-helmetStripe-spots>` → the two bombers read as distinct identities at a glance, not just 'two coloured robots'. Manual QA bar, documented in the kaboom-crew README.
OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
Normal maps / image textures / UV mapping — visual-style.md §4.3 (no PBR / HDRI / image baking).
Per-accessory texturing — accessories stay solid-coloured for silhouette discipline.
Animated patterns (e.g. flowing emissive lines) — separate shader profile, separate story.
Decal placement editor — anchors are fixed in code, not authorable.
More decal types beyond the 3 — design budget; future decals (`backplate`, `eyeDot`, `armBand` per the deferred-list in GDP-2026-05-21-004) ship one at a time when a specific moment needs them.
